validation.name: determinism and independence
validation.criterion: two scheduler instances stepped in alternation give bit-identical results

deviations.what: the per-substep scalars (raw time, sigma, interpolation index and weights, substep counts) are computed on the host in NumPy float32; only the tensor updates run in MLX
deviations.why: They depend only on the schedule and are the same for every batch element (the step takes one timestep). NumPy float32 performs the same correctly rounded IEEE operations as the reference's float32 torch scalars, including round-half-to-even for the substep count, and avoids device division differences. Results are bit-identical to the reference.

deviations.what: the spec's determinism case 'stochastic_sampling=false' has no counterpart: PiflowScheduler in diffusers 0.42.1 has no stochastic branch
deviations.why: The released scheduler_config.json carries stochastic_sampling, use_dynamic_shifting and other FlowMatch keys; the reference ignores them (with a warning), and from_config ignores them the same way. Determinism is tested directly instead.

deviations.what: step returns the sample, not a PiflowSchedulerOutput; set_timesteps takes only num_inference_steps
deviations.why: the reference rejects custom sigmas, mu and timesteps anyway; the pipeline (spec 09) is the only caller

follow_ups: Spec 09 runs the real 10-step loop and compares latents with the diffusers pipeline from the same noise.

architecture_notes.note: 10 PiFlow steps (124 policy evaluations) on Smoke video latents take 23 ms in MLX, audio 6 ms; the DiT forward is 1.45 s per step.
architecture_notes.optimization: None needed; host-side NumPy scalars avoid device syncs.

architecture_notes.note: PiFlow needs n_grid = 10 predictions per channel, so the DiT heads output 160 video and 400 audio channels; the extra projection width is negligible next to attention.
